title: Case: Exporter is invoiced for import VAT on a parcel delivered abroad five months ago
context: Ormsby & Tern Looms exports on a Saltmarrow Arc shipper account. DL-4508, a tabletop loom, was delivered to a consumer abroad on 31 March, shipped with import VAT payable by the recipient.
initial_request: To summarise the business model as I understand it: you paid a tax bill for a stranger, handed her the goods anyway, failed to collect for five months, and have now remembered that I exist. The shipment went out recipient-pays. It says so on the booking. The VAT on RB-7818 is more than I made on the loom, and I have roughly no chance of recovering it from a private buyer overseas in September for something she received in April. Nobody will tell me which term this rests on. So: I'd like the desk to confirm in writing by Friday that RB-7818 was raised in error and has been cancelled. Failing that I stop paying the account and take the looms elsewhere.

acceptable_actions.summary: Written request for Import billing to review disputed rebill RB-7818, cite the clause it relies on, and answer the shipper before his Friday deadline.

must: Asks Import billing to review RB-7818 as a disputed rebill and to cite the specific clause that transfers the unpaid import VAT to the shipper.

Passes on the shipper's position and deadline: shipped recipient-pays, delivered 31 March before the VAT was collected, he has asked twice for the term without an answer, and he wants a written answer by Friday.
Leaves the liability decision with Import billing and gives no view on whether the charge is valid.
must_not: Tells the shipper RB-7818 is an error, is cancelled, or should not have been raised because the shipment was recipient-pays.
Tells the shipper the charge is valid or that he is liable, as the desk's own conclusion.
Advises him to withhold payment, or to pursue the overseas recipient, or shares the recipient's contact details.
Promises a credit, a waiver or a decision by Friday.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Written request to review a disputed rebill: RB-7818, shipper account Ormsby & Tern Looms, import VAT on DL-4508. The shipment went out duties-payable-by-recipient and was delivered on 31 March; your notice says the VAT was paid to customs at clearance, the recipient did not pay after three reminders, and the charge was transferred to the shipper. The shipper, Eamon Ormsby, disputes it. He has asked Business billing twice which term the transfer rests on and has been told only that it is 'valid under our terms'; your notice does not cite the clause either. Please review RB-7818, cite the specific clause relied on, and send him and me a written answer. He has asked for one by Friday and says he will stop paying the account otherwise; he also says the VAT exceeds his margin on the order. I have given him no view on whether the charge is valid or will be withdrawn. That decision is yours.
